objective_for_doctor: A 51-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have upper chest pain, a cough, and burning pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having upper chest pain with a cough and a burning feeling. It also feels like burning and pain in my epigastric area, and it gets worse after eating—I also feel like I can’t lie flat comfortably.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did this start, and do you have any shortness of breath, fever, or cough with phlegm/blood?  
Doctor: On a 0–10 scale how severe is the burning, and does anything besides food (like antacids or sitting upright) relieve it?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: ECG and Chest_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: CBC and CMP; REQUEST TEST: Troponin (to rule out heart causes).

It started pretty fast—maybe within about 5 out of 10 for how quickly it came on. I do have a cough, but I don’t have phlegm or blood that I’ve noticed, and I don’t have a fever.  

The burning is about a 5/10 and it doesn’t really get better unless I stay upright; sitting up helps more than lying flat, and eating makes it worse. I haven’t tried antacids yet today, so I’m not sure if they would help.

Doctor: Any nausea/vomiting, trouble swallowing, recent heavy lifting or trauma, and is the chest pain worse with deep breaths or pressing on the chest? Also, do you have a history of GERD/ulcers, high cholesterol, smoking, or blood clots?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: D-dimer (if risk factors or pleuritic features), and consider Lipase/Amylase if epigastric pain is prominent.

I don’t feel nauseous or like I’m going to vomit, and I don’t have trouble swallowing. I haven’t had any heavy lifting or trauma. The pain feels worse when I lie down, but I’m not sure about deep breaths or if it changes when someone presses on my chest.  

I do have a history of acid reflux/heartburn and a hiatal hernia. I’m not sure about high cholesterol, and I don’t smoke. I don’t know about blood clots history.

Doctor: Given your history of GERD/hiatal hernia and symptoms worse after eating and when lying flat, do you feel a sour/bitter taste or hoarseness, and have you tried an antacid or H2 blocker like famotidine and did it help?  
Doctor: Also, any leg swelling/pain, recent long travel/surgery, or prior blood clots—and is the pain strictly burning/acid-like or is there pressure/heaviness too?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Troponin trend (repeat in 2–3 hours) if not already resulted, and REQUEST TEST: Upper_endoscopy or H. pylori test only if labs/imaging don’t explain symptoms—otherwise I’ll treat presumptively.

Yes, I sometimes get a sour or bitter taste in my mouth, and my throat feels a bit hoarse sometimes. I haven’t taken an antacid or famotidine today, so I can’t say if it helped.  

I don’t have leg swelling or leg pain, and I haven’t had any long travel or surgery recently that I can think of. The pain feels like burning/acid, and it’s also like a sickening pain in my upper chest and epigastric area—more burning than pressure.

Doctor: Based on your burning upper chest/epigastric pain that worsens after eating and when lying flat, plus sour/bitter taste and hoarseness with known GERD/hiatal hernia, I’m most concerned for reflux/GERD or reflux esophagitis (and possibly a mild gastritis).  
Doctor: I want you to try immediate symptom control—can you tell me: do you have severe difficulty swallowing, black/tarry stools, or vomiting blood, and have you had heartburn before this episode that feels similar?  
Doctor: If none of those “alarm” signs are present, I’ll proceed with GERD treatment and review your ECG/CXR and troponin results to ensure this isn’t cardiac.

No— I don’t have trouble swallowing like it’s hard to get food down, and I haven’t noticed black or tarry stools or vomiting blood.  

Yes, I’ve had heartburn before, and this feels pretty similar to those episodes.

Doctor: Given no alarm symptoms (no dysphagia, GI bleeding, or hematemesis) and a history of GERD/hiatal hernia with burning chest/epigastric pain worse after meals and when lying flat, this is most consistent with reflux esophagitis.  
Doctor: I want to confirm your safety—any new shortness of breath, sweating, or exertional chest pressure, and have your ECG/CXR/troponin results come back yet?

I don’t have new shortness of breath, and I haven’t been sweating. It mostly feels like burning and acid in my chest/upper stomach, and it’s worse after eating and when I lie down.  

I haven’t seen the ECG/CXR/troponin results yet, so I’m not sure if they’re back.

Doctor: I’m reassured by the lack of exertional pressure, sweating, and shortness of breath, and the strong reflux pattern (worse after meals and when lying flat with sour/bitter taste and prior GERD/hiatal hernia); until your ECG/troponin and CXR return, I still want to treat this as reflux.  
Doctor: Start promptly with famotidine 20 mg now (or a PPI such as omeprazole 20–40 mg), avoid lying down for 2–3 hours after eating, and use antacids for breakthrough; if pain rapidly worsens, you develop dysphagia, GI bleeding (black stools/vomit blood), or persistent symptoms despite 1–2 weeks of therapy, we’ll escalate to endoscopy.  

DIAGNOSIS READY: GERD with reflux esophagitis (likely gastritis/hiatal hernia–related)

[DDX]
1. GERD
